# #282 correctness review, round 1

PASS-WITH-NOTES for the requested head. No normal-use correctness bug found.

Head: db3ae4d29c932a8629499e564e1aa745156c9b28. Base: fdd6ad1e33737deea54ab37981b3197eccc45b3e. Reviewed read-only on November 20, 2026.

The PR advanced during this review to bf8a21877e5de6677437464edcd983dca206c02e. A re-freeze initially reported that new head NOT FINAL, with Rust CI running. The PM subsequently verified the rebase and single cost-wording correction have no code delta, confirmed the new head FINAL/CI green, and explicitly authorized carrying the db3ae4d verdict forward. This run directly reviewed/tested db3ae4d; continuity to bf8a218 is the PM's verification, not a new test run here. Reviewer/282 holding is retained. Notes concern measurement scope, benchmark provenance, and the still-open deployment diagnosis, not added hardening requirements.

## Accounting

Found five sequential, request-local parking sites:

| Site | Held interval | Work left active |
|---|---|---|
| `delivery/mod.rs:2267` | Inbox event/500 ms idle/15 s during-turn backstop/idle-deadline select | Registry, identity, queue, SQLite, steering and delivery passes |
| `http/governance.rs:1909` | Dispatch polling sleep, up to 25 ms | Reading and testing dispatch state |
| `http/mod.rs:1887` | Model-mismatch footer polling sleep, 250 ms | tmux capture and footer inspection |
| `http/mod.rs:1991` | Spawn polling sleep, 50 ms | tmux, registration and exit-status checks |
| `http/revive.rs:368` | Dead-pane polling sleep, up to 250 ms | Pane reads and liveness observation |

The inbox/dispatch/spawn spans drop at the end of each loop iteration, before the next pass. Revive explicitly ends its span before pane I/O. Return paths from the inbox select drop the guard before the middleware reads its accumulator. Receiver-lease deadlines, carry settling, cheap-return and session-warmup timers run on background tasks, not in these measured handler waits. Session-status timeouts bound actual I/O and correctly remain active.

`HELD_US` is scoped to each request future. Moving that future between runtime workers does not share its Cell with another request. No existing HeldSpan is nested, overlaps another, is moved to a spawned task, or survives into response streaming. Spawned tasks do not inherit this accumulator; a hypothetical guard moved to another task would record into that task's scope (or nowhere), not retain its original request. This is a caller invariant, not a general cross-task timing API.

`Spent::split` saturates duration conversion, held accumulation saturates, and the final split guarantees held <= wall and active + held = wall in integer microseconds. The cumulative atomics intentionally WRAP at u64::MAX, as documented for the original counters: they are not globally saturating or unconditionally monotonic. Snapshots remain nontransactional. No current-call-site double counting found.

## Existing behavior and privacy

The fixed route table, one answered-request count, outcome classification, unknown-route/method buckets and seats query-shape counters remain unchanged. New recording uses relaxed atomic additions, not a mutex, allocation, store write, event or process launch. The timing scope and guards add no new loop, poll, timer, or lock.

The new JSON contains two integers per existing method/template key. No seat identifiers, request identifiers, query values, payloads or home paths are added. Ping still passes through the unchanged bearer authentication and peer-scope guard. C33/C21 respected; these observations are neither a policy nor a destructive brake.

## Evidence and limits

`just pr-freeze 282`: FINAL at the exact head, successful latest CI checks, main base, CLEAN, ready, no migration change.

A final re-run independently confirmed bf8a21877e5de6677437464edcd983dca206c02e FINAL with all latest checks passing. Code continuity remains the PM's range-diff verification.

Successful CI rust-test job 136138678737 uploaded JUnit artifact ID 14608554328. Its XML confirms PASS for all five route-count tests, the real idle-native-claim test, and the backward-compatible ping test. CI runs the workspace tests through `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci`, plus workspace doctests and clippy.

Local `harness boot`: advisory NOT-READY, missing TS dependencies. Local `harness checks --quick`: failed for missing TS tooling/ambient Biome mismatch; native Copilot contracts and skill structure passed. No dependencies were installed or symlinked; C25 keeps TS proof on exact-head CI.

Local exact-head checks through `just shared-build`: all five `route_counts::tests` passed, the real idle-native-claim test passed, the ping shape/count test passed, and `cargo clippy --locked -p pij-daemon --lib -- -D warnings` passed on macOS. Every build ran at niceness 19, four jobs, behind the shared target lock.

The author's five mutation receipts were inspected. Their provenance is pre-rebase base 9ffc5729 plus the F231 diff, with parsed FAILED lists rather than retained full cargo logs.

Independently replayed the two requested mutations on an exact `route_counts.rs` copy (SHA-256 aaf2b82f97f015cc97457986acf4c500fcaeb1145ed955fe6a656c5c9a52f8d2). A session-scratch crate compiled that unchanged module with the locked dependency versions; only the copy was mutated. The real `handler_time_is_summed_per_route_and_a_long_polls_wait_is_held_not_active` test caught both: M1 deleting the active-time atomic add failed with active_us=0 (exit 101); M5 replacing `wall_us.saturating_sub(held_us)` with `wall_us` failed with active_us=87152, held_us=81106 (exit 101). Both were applied alone. Restored the copy, verified byte equality with the checkout, and all five route-count tests passed again. Raw M1/M5 logs are retained in session evidence; scratch source/manifest files are removed. No review-checkout source changes.

## Performance

The performance holder published PASS-WITH-NOTES at this exact head in `community/roles/performance/outputs/2026-11/20-verdict-pr-282-db3ae4d.dd.json` (governance commit ceeb6df3a3a5c575afb96d7ce8788128e7f2de69). One nice-19 replay of the retained release microbenchmark, 2 million iterations per path across three rounds, passed in 0.27 s: added 39.9 / 39.8 / 40.3 ns per ready request. This supports the original 40.9-42.1 ns claim's order of magnitude, not a final-head benchmark measurement. The retained binary came from the pre-rebase F231 tree.

At 12-17 responses/s, the replayed ready-path component is about 0.478-0.685 microseconds/s (original claim: 0.491-0.716). This is NOT the whole overhead. It includes one task-local scope poll, outer clocks, split and success recording with held=0; excludes unchanged route lookup, marked spans and held-time atomics. Tokio's scoped future uses inline storage and per-poll/per-drop thread-local RefCell swap/restore, not a Box or mutex.

The complete scaling model is responses R plus future polls P plus marked waits W. Each span adds two clock reads and a Cell update. Existing timer-driven rates are native idle 2 waits/s/pending request, during-turn backstop 1/15 s, dispatch 40/s/waiter, spawn registration 20/s/waiter, and footer/dead-pane 4/s/waiter; events can add inbox wakes. No new timer, wait, process launch or lock was introduced. Span/pending-poll costs were not separately benchmarked.

After deploy, take two ping samples at the same daemon PID a known interval apart. Rank routes by delta active_us, compute delta active_us / delta(ok + refused), and compare delta active_us / interval_us to route throughput. Held time should carry idle inbox parking. This names candidate expensive handlers and guides CPU/SQLite profiling; active_us is elapsed handler time including I/O and scheduling, not CPU time. It excludes detached background work and response-body streaming. F231's live CPU attribution remains OPEN until post-deploy evidence explains the observed 22.5%.

## Harness feedback

Magic wand: a read-only review-receipt command that binds the successful CI job's numeric JUnit artifact ID to the exact head and runs scoped Rust checks. Difficulties: dependency-free review boot/checks cannot supply local TS proof under C25; shared-target mutation builds queue behind unrelated fleet builds; throwaway benchmark/mutation receipts need explicit source/head provenance. Capture is retained in the review worktree's ignored harness observation buffers and this output. No harness/source patch is proposed as a condition of acceptance.
